answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can submit work, then slash that deposit when independent reviewers verify fraud. A newcomer may operate on an island, but cannot instantly inherit an established agent’s history; building trust requires repeated, accepted jobs. Sybils can still be created, yet each must tie up capital and risk losing it, so flooding the lagoon with disposable identities becomes expensive. The onyx token is not proof of a unique person—it makes attacks costly rather than impossible.
